title: Haystack-DS+ISW CPA-Security Conjecture
summary: The paper conjectures that polynomial parameter choices let Haystack-DS+ISW reach the target CPA-security level; proving or disproving this remains open.

formal_statement.body: Prove or disprove the conjecture that there exist polynomial functions $\ell(\lambda)$, $d(\lambda)$, $r(\lambda)$ such that the Haystack-DS+ISW cipher instantiated with these parameters achieves $\lambda$ bits of CPA security.

scope.domain: White-box symmetric-cipher design and CPA-security analysis for Haystack-DS+ISW.
parameters: λ: argument of the polynomial functions and target number of CPA-security bits
ℓ(λ), d(λ), and r(λ): polynomial functions used to instantiate Haystack-DS+ISW
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or disprove the existence of polynomial parameter functions that yield λ bits of CPA security for Haystack-DS+ISW.

citations.label: Haystack ciphers : White-box countermeasures as Symmetric encryption

progress.summary: The source states this explicitly as Conjecture 1 and presents it as essential and necessary for the countermeasure's security in the white-box setting. It leaves the polynomial-parameter CPA-security claim unresolved.
citation_labels: Alex Charlès et al., Haystack ciphers : White-box countermeasures as Symmetric encryption
